Definitional, Revision and Referral Notes

Statistical Notes
Data items are classified according to the Classification of Individual Consumption by Purpose Adapted to the Needs of Harmonized Indices of Consumer Prices (2000).
For more details please go to web page: http://ec.europa.eu/eurostat/ramon/nomenclatures/index.cfm?TargetUrl=LST_CLS_DLD&StrNom=HICP_2000&StrLanguageCode=EN&StrLayoutCode=HIERARCHIC
Definitional Notes
The CPI is a measure of consumer price inflation produced to international standards and in line with European regulations. First published in 1997 as the Harmonized Index of Consumer Prices (HICP), the CPI is the inflation measure used in the Government’s target for inflation. The CPI is also used for purposes such as up rating pensions, wages and benefits and can aid in the understanding of inflation on family budgets. More methodological explanation can be found on web page: www.ons.gov.uk/…

Harmonized CPI United Kingdom

Harmonized Indexes of Consumer Prices (HICPs) are harmonized inflation figures required under Article 121 of the Treaty of Amsterdam. They are designed for international comparison of consumer price inflation. HICPs are compiled on the basis of a legislated methodology, binding for all Member States. The focus is on quality and comparability among the indices of different countries as well as on their relative movements. The HICPs aim at measuring pure price changes using a harmonized methodology. As from January 2006, the HICP is calculated with the new base year 2005=100 instead of 1996=100. The change of the base year is due to the Commission Regulation No.1708/2005, which sets the year 2005 as the new common reference period for all HICPs of the Member States of the E.U.
